criteria.evidence: K82 repairs the published catalog’s binding defect without changing instruction semantics or narrowing north-star capabilities. Its exception is confined to recipes with serialized bare-name formals.
criteria.change: Optional, §11.1 K82: add “Named-interface binding changes recipe admission and name resolution only; source-instruction semantics remain unchanged.”

criteria.evidence: Reproducing generate.py --check confirms 54 named-interface recipes, 20 invoke sites, 86 finite instances and the published envelope hash. The width rule correctly permits partial reads without inferring widths from accessed indices; no false technical premise was found.
criteria.change: Optional, §11.1 K82: add “Classification uses the serialized parameters list before any internal normalization of bare names into typed integer formals.”

criteria.evidence: Bindings resolve from lexical expansion environments, preserving the machine’s prohibition on scheduling decisions derived from quantum values. Wider interface lists contribute untouched wires rather than additional operations.
criteria.change: Optional, §11.1 K82: add “Interface discovery and binding do not inspect the quantum values carried by the resolved wires.”

criteria.evidence: Consumers receive a public binding rule instead of depending on either consumer’s undocumented capture behavior. K26/K27 preserve wire identity and lifetime obligations, while K77 remains a separate explicit context channel.
criteria.change: Optional, §11.1 K82: add “A consumer MUST NOT supplement this interface with other caller bindings.”

criteria.evidence: The repair operates entirely within the expansion-library contract and adds no LLVM, frontend or language dependency. Existing source capabilities retain their constructions.
criteria.change: Optional, §11.1 K82: add “Producers need no additional source operands for named-interface binding; the invoking lexical environment supplies the specified wire actuals.”

criteria.evidence: The vector covers closure rejection, capture, transitive interfaces, bounds, regions and live declarations. Its normalized edge digests omit controls and allocation metadata, so they do not independently demonstrate every identity-preservation assertion relevant to scheduling.
criteria.change: In §15’s K82 vector description, add “Supplemental vectors record inherited controls, leaf ordinals and allocation width, class, state and occurrence identity.” Include forward/inverse expectations retaining each forward ordinal and allocation identity.

criteria.evidence: K82 makes no unsupported novelty claim. Explicit free-wire interfaces and lexical captures are coherent binding conventions, and the change leaves K20’s phase-sensitive quantum obligations intact.
criteria.change: Optional, §11.1 K82: add “Named-interface recipes retain all K20 witness obligations, including identity on unread interface wires.”

criteria.evidence: The paragraph supplies actionable rules for eligibility, lookup, widths, direct instantiation and allocation scope. “Every K22 template … is closed” is consistent with K22 when saved captures count as bindings, but stating that explicitly would prevent misreading.
criteria.change: After the closed-template sentence in §11.1 K82, add “Names bound in a body’s or template’s saved lexical capture remain bound; closed forbids importing additional bindings from the splice or apply site.”

suggestions: §15: add “Supplemental K82 vectors preserve inherited controls, leaf ordinals and complete allocation metadata across forward and inverse traversal.” For an allocated scratch lifetime, the inverse must retain its forward occurrence identity and visit its forward ordinals in reverse order.

§11.1 K82: add “Names bound in a saved lexical capture remain bound; closed forbids importing additional splice-site or apply-site bindings.” The existing bare-template witness must continue emitting X on captured b[0], even when the application environment binds b to a different wire.
path_to_accept: No blocking changes are required. To raise C8 from 4 to 5, explicitly distinguish preserved lexical captures from forbidden additional caller imports using the sentence supplied above.
summary: Accept K82. The catalog counts and unchanged envelope hash reproduce, and the proposed rule resolves the binding defect while preserving typed closure, captures, lifetime checks, quantum witness obligations, invocation context and occurrence numbering. Reported consumer implementation failures do not invalidate the proposed normative rule.
